files.prompt: Use case: director review Production Design Target for a strategy game unit, a clean 3D model appearance render. Create one single finished, plausible LEGO-built vehicle on a neutral pale warm-gray studio background, three-quarter front view, no text, no labels, no watermark. The unit is Solar Explorer, faithfully adapted from the completed 2001 LEGO Life on Mars set 7315. Preserve the recognizable source assembly: a very long low white/light-gray modular carrier; foremost detachable compact cockpit craft with low pointed wedge nose and broad blue side plates; central habitation/cargo module dominated by one large curved translucent dark-red canopy with a clear repeating hexagonal honeycomb pattern; a compact rear service module organized around an open circular white frame with red dome and two small red fins; a small four-wheel scout rover attached as a distinct subordinate pod. Visible game adaptation: add exactly six modest rugged black wheels as three paired axles, low and tucked under the long carrier, clearly secondary to the source modules; visible simple white/medium-blue structural carrier spine and standardized couplers between modules; add a small fold-down stabilizer at the rear service module, restrained and subordinate. Keep classic Life on Mars white, medium-blue, dark gray and red source palette, exposed brick-built construction and toy-like LEGO part logic; crisp seams, sturdy geometry, readable RTS-scale silhouette. Do not turn it into a generic sci-fi bus, aircraft, tank, giant truck or modern vehicle. No weapons, no extra modules, no extra wheels, no solar panel wings, no loose crew. The canopy, cockpit craft, rover, and circular rear frame must remain individually legible. Present an appearance target, not a diagram or parts breakdown.

revisions.prompt: Make a precise cleanup edit to this proposed LEGO Life on Mars Solar Explorer T083 target. Preserve the long low six-wheel carrier, front detachable wedge cockpit, ONE central curved red honeycomb habitat canopy, the compact separate rear service module with its circular frame, small red dome and paired short fins, plus the separate small rover. Remove both tall white-and-blue vertical towers/pylons above the rear service module; the source has only two small fins, each less than half the circular frame height. Remove tall red antenna cylinders and extraneous stacked rear structures. Keep all upper modules low and compact so the honeycomb canopy remains the highest large mass. Retain the proposed six modest wheels, exposed white/blue carrier spine, source palette and neutral background. Do not duplicate any canopy, ring, or module. No new structure, no weapons, no solar wings, no text.
